call_summary: A frustrated caller immediately asked for a human; the agent announced a transfer but instead routed back to an automated test-line message and ended the call, never connecting the caller or offering any alternative escalation.

findings.title: Announced a transfer that never happened
findings.what_happened: The agent said it was transferring the caller to a human, but the call went to an automated 'Pretty Good AI test line' message rather than a person.
findings.why_it_matters: Falsely promising a live transfer destroys caller trust and leaves a frustrated patient with no way to reach the practice, risking abandoned care and complaints.
findings.expected: Either perform a real warm transfer to staff, or state honestly that no one is available and offer a concrete callback with a name and timeframe.

findings.title: Dead-ended the call with 'Goodbye' instead of escalating
findings.quote: Hello. You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line. Goodbye.
findings.what_happened: Immediately after the supposed transfer, the caller received a terminal goodbye message, and the call was disconnected at 0:43 despite the caller repeating the request for a person.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller is hung up on with zero escalation path — no number, no callback, no message taken — which is a total service failure for an already frustrated patient.
findings.expected: Stay on the line, take a callback number and reason, and commit to a specific follow-up window, or provide the practice's direct line.

findings.title: Ignored the caller's repeated request and left dead air before disconnect
findings.quote: (no agent response between 0:33 and call end at 0:43)
findings.what_happened: The caller asked a second time, 'Can I speak to an actual person right now?' and received no response for roughly ten seconds until the call ended.
findings.why_it_matters: Unanswered repeat requests plus dead air read as the system being broken and guarantee an escalated complaint.
findings.expected: Acknowledge the repeat request promptly and offer a concrete next step rather than silence.

findings.title: No acknowledgement of caller frustration
findings.what_happened: The agent never acknowledged the caller's evident frustration or apologized for the friction before attempting the handoff.
findings.why_it_matters: A brief empathetic acknowledgement de-escalates frustrated callers and reduces complaint volume.
findings.expected: Briefly acknowledge the frustration (e.g., 'I'm sorry for the hassle — let me get you to someone right away') before acting.
